notes: Story has zero acceptance criteria and a description that merely repeats the title. 'Live Preview of Content in CMS' is a novel capability — the codebase currently has no live-preview mechanism. The central integration point is useContent (236 callers), which is the sole hook through which all Contentstack content flows. VCs are derived from the description alone and are framed at our boundary since Contentstack services are unreachable at test time. This story is underspecified — product should define what 'live preview' means (WebSocket push? polling? Contentstack's built-in Live Preview SDK? manual refresh?) before implementation begins.

notes: Openspec produced zero ACs and correctly flagged the story as underspecified. I added 12 acceptance criteria from scratch based on the story title, the listed technical files (useContent, ContentstackImage, ContentstackLink, contentstack service), and reasonable expectations for a CMS live-preview feature. AC-1/2 cover core happy-path preview behavior. AC-3 ensures preview mode is opt-in and doesn't affect production. AC-4/5 cover connection lifecycle (disconnect indicator + auto-reconnect). AC-6 covers malformed data resilience. AC-7/8 address the two specific component types listed in technical notes. AC-9 covers accessibility (screen-reader announcement of dynamic content). AC-10 prevents torn-write visual glitches. AC-11 covers entry-switching in the CMS. AC-12 covers a security boundary (no draft content leakage). All criteria are framed as observable outcomes without prescribing implementation.
